name: Phoebe
title: Deacon in Cenchreae
summary: Phoebe was a deacon in the church at Cenchreae, a port city near Corinth. She was commended by Paul to the church in Rome and described as one who had been a help to many, including Paul himself. She likely carried Paul's letter to the Romans.

keyEvents.title: Paul Commends Phoebe
keyEvents.description: Paul commends Phoebe to the church in Rome and asks them to receive her in the Lord in a way worthy of the saints.

keyEvents.title: Phoebe as Church Deacon
keyEvents.description: Phoebe is referred to as a deacon (servant) in the church at Cenchreae, showing that she held an recognized ministry in the early church.

keyEvents.title: Phoebe as Benefactor and Protector
keyEvents.description: Paul describes Phoebe as one who has been a benefactor and protector (prostatis) for many, including himself, suggesting that she used her resources to support the Christian movement.

keyEvents.title: Bearer of the Letter to the Romans
keyEvents.description: Based on Paul's recommendation, it is believed that Phoebe was the trusted messenger who delivered the Letter to the Romans from Corinth to the church in Rome, a task of great significance.

keyEvents.title: Phoebe in the Cenchreae Church
keyEvents.description: Cenchreae was one of Corinth's port cities, and Phoebe served faithfully in this church, which was part of the broader Christian network Paul had established in the region of Achaia.
